tagline: A tiny design system with live playgrounds

hero.kicker: Design system · three components · zero excuses
hero.headline: Flip a prop. Watch it change.
hero.intro: Vitrine is the component kit behind our products, published the day it became real. Every component gets a live playground: set the props with real controls, watch the specimen respond, and copy the exact markup that reproduces what you see.
hero.stageCaption: Rendered live by the same components the playgrounds document — nothing here is a screenshot.

items.title: Small on purpose
items.body: A component joins the kit when three production screens need it, and not a screen sooner. That rule has rejected more components than it has admitted — and the kit fits in one afternoon because of it.

items.title: Props are the API
items.body: No utility-class overrides, no theme forks, no local CSS patches. If a variation matters, it becomes a documented prop with a visible default. Everything else is a proposal, not a workaround.

items.title: The snippet is the truth
items.body: Each playground writes the exact markup that reproduces its preview, omitting props that sit at their defaults. What you copy is what ships — nothing hides in a wrapper class.

componentIndex.heading: Three components, honestly documented
componentIndex.intro: Each page pairs a live playground with a prop table and usage notes. Open one, flip the props, and take the snippet with you — your last configuration is remembered on this device.

faq.heading: What teams ask before adopting Vitrine

items.question: Why does the kit ship only three components?
items.answer: Because three are real. A component enters Vitrine once three production screens need it — that rule has killed more components than it has admitted, and it is why the whole kit can be learned in an afternoon.

items.question: Can I override a component with my own CSS?
items.answer: Please don't. Every supported variation is a prop, and the playground shows the full set. If a design needs something the props cannot express, that is a proposal for a new prop — not a local override that the next release silently breaks.

items.question: Does the playground save my configuration?
items.answer: Yes, in this browser. Each playground stores the last props you set on your device and restores them when you come back. Nothing leaves your machine, and Reset props returns the playground to its documented starting point.

items.question: How do I propose a new component or prop?
items.answer: Bring three screens that need it, plus the markup you wish you could write. The core team reviews proposals every Thursday; accepted work lands with a playground, a prop table, and usage notes like everything else here.

items.question: Which stack do the snippets target?
items.answer: Vue 3 single-file components with TypeScript props. The snippet under each preview is plain template markup — paste it into any SFC that imports the kit and it renders exactly what the playground showed you.

footer.line: The component kit behind our products — documented in the open, one honest playground per component.
footer.editNote: Vitrine ships as a template with demo content. The system name, copy, and FAQs live in src/data/site.json; the components and their props in src/data/components.ts.
